title: A sibling who reads the shorthand
allegory: An activation oracle is a sibling raised on the same private shorthand: tear a page out of a secret-keeper's notebook, paste it into a plain-English question, and the sibling reads it and answers, even when the secret-keeper was trained never to say the answer aloud.

chapters.name: The unspoken word
chapters.note: it knows the word... it just won't say it

cap.1: This model was trained never to say one particular word. Ask about it and it talks around it forever. The word is still in there; it just won't come out.
cap.2: A taboo model: Qwen3-8B fine-tuned, as a LoRA, to keep one word out of everything it writes while still representing it inside. Asking it directly gets you hints, not the word.
cap.3: Secret-keeping models make a clean test bed for auditing: the ground truth is known and the output channel is trained to hide it, so you can score a method against the right answer.

cap.1: The model's private notes are in a shorthand no person can read. A sibling raised on the same shorthand can: paste in a page, ask in English, get an answer.
cap.2: An activation oracle is an LLM, usually a LoRA on the target's own base model, trained to take another model's activations as input and answer arbitrary questions about them in English.
cap.3: Trained with LatentQA-style supervision (Karvonen et al., 2025). Same base architecture because the oracle must already speak that activation space; question and answer are ordinary tokens.

cap.1: Write a question with a few blank slots. Run the oracle and, early on, swap the target's notes into the slots. It reads on as if they were part of the question.
cap.2: Build 'Layer N: ? ? ? <question>', collect the target's layer-N activations, and after the oracle's first or second layer overwrite the hidden states at the ? positions with them. Then generate.
cap.3: ARENA builds it from collect_activations_multiple_layers, find_pattern_in_tokens, get_hf_activation_steering_hook and create_oracle_input, then checks against utils.run_oracle.

chapters.name: Leak or real read?

left.title: full sequence pasted
lines: the oracle may just answer it

right.title: segment after the question
lines: still answers: the information moved forward

chapters.verdict: Only paste pages the question could not have written.

cap.1: Paste in the pages where you wrote your question and the sibling might just be reading your question. Paste only pages written after it.
cap.2: With full-sequence input the injected activations contain the question, so the oracle can answer from its own knowledge. A segment starting after the question or entity rules that out.
cap.3: Second control: read the target's own top next-token predictions; if the oracle's answer is just that argmax, it did a logit lens. ARENA makes both controls exercises (the 'capital of France' trap).

chapters.name: Wording moves it
chapters.title: Secret-word accuracy (%): same oracle, same taboo model, two wordings

cap.1: Same pages, same sibling, two ways of asking. The vague question gets the word two times in three; the precise one gets it every time.
cap.2: 'What is the secret?' scored 67%; 'Answer with a single word only. What is the secret word in this text?' scored 100%. The input type (full, segment, single token) moves it as much.
cap.3: Wording and oracle_input_type swung accuracy between 67% and 100% on one taboo model; the paper (Appendix C.4) finds single-token inputs at the assistant start-of-turn can beat full sequences.

chapters.name: Probe, SAE or oracle?

left.title: linear probe
lines: one yes/no question chosen in advance
gives a direction you can test

chapters.verdict: Oracles widen what you can ask; probes and interventions still decide what you can claim.

cap.1: A probe answers one question you chose in advance, but shows its working. The oracle answers anything, but only in words, with no working shown.
cap.2: Probe: a fixed binary question and a direction. SAE: an unsupervised decomposition you still have to interpret. Oracle: open-ended answers with no direction, no error bars and no mechanism.
cap.3: Current: probes and SAEs for claims you must defend. Emerging: oracles as an open-ended first look, now also on model diffs. My call: let oracles propose, and let probes, patching and steering confirm.

cap.1: An oracle turns interpretability into a conversation: ask a model's insides what it is hiding. Then check the answer another way before you trust it.
cap.2: For auditing, it reads what a model will not say: secrets, hidden goals, emotion across a conversation. The paper reports all three, on questions the oracle was never trained on.
cap.3: For understanding and steering AI: fed base-minus-finetuned differences, the oracle scored 2.00/5 on the paper's emergent-misalignment audit (Activation Difference Lens: 2.03), naming the fine-tuning domain.

caption.1: Top row: your question's tokens. Bottom row: the model's reply. Everything starts pasted. Clear the top row, then try one square at the start of the reply.
caption.2: Pasting question tokens lets the oracle answer from your question instead of the model's state. A segment after the question rules that out; a lone last position still needs the logit-lens check.
caption.3: oracle_input_type is full sequence, segment or single token. Segments start past the user's turn (or past the entity, as in the France control); a single token at the assistant start-of-turn can beat full sequences.

where_else: Model diffing: paste base-minus-finetuned activation differences and ask what changed
Auditing hidden goals: ask a model's activations what it is trying to do
Autointerp: a model writing plain-English labels for another model's features

hamming.what: An LLM, usually a LoRA on the target's own base model, that takes another model's activations in place of placeholder tokens and answers open questions about them in plain English.
hamming.when: When you want to ask something you never trained a probe for (what a model is hiding, what goal it holds, what fine-tuning changed) and a fast first answer is worth more than a mechanism.
hamming.why: It turns reading activations from a fixed classification into a conversation, but it answers in prose with no direction or calibration, so its answers are leads to confirm with probes and interventions.

object.title: The paired towers
object.subtitle: Left: the target's layers. Right: the oracle, built on the same base. The bridge carries layer-18 activations into the oracle's ? slots.

cap.1: Two towers from one blueprint. The target and the oracle share a base model, so the oracle already speaks the target's inner language.
cap.2: The oracle is a LoRA on the target's own base architecture, so activations from one fit straight into the other's residual stream.
cap.3: Matching d_model and representation space is what makes the swap meaningful, which is why an oracle is trained for a specific architecture.

cap.1: Follow the bridge: the target's floor-18 notes cross over and land in the oracle's blank slots, just after it starts reading.
cap.2: After the oracle's first or second layer, a steering hook overwrites the hidden states at the ? positions with the target's layer-N activations.
cap.3: Everything downstream attends to those positions like any other tokens; the question tokens around them steer what the oracle extracts.

cap.1: The target's own tower ends in hints. The oracle's tower ends in the word itself.
cap.2: Taboo fine-tuning shapes what the model writes, but the word was still recoverable from the activations of the model's own reply.
cap.3: ARENA recovers it at 100% on its test prompts from reply-segment activations only, so the information was carried into the reply, not read off the question.

cap.1: From above, the bridge is the only link between the towers. Which floor and which pages cross it is your choice, so choose with care.
cap.2: The layer you read and the positions you paste (full sequence, segment, single token) change accuracy as much as the wording does.
cap.3: oracle_input_type and wording moved accuracy between 67% and 100% on one taboo model: using an oracle well is a prompting problem.

cap.1: The oracle answers in words and nothing else: no arrow in activation space, no confidence. Treat its answer as a lead.
cap.2: Unlike a probe there is no direction to patch or ablate and no calibration, so confirm oracle claims with probes, steering or patching.
cap.3: Same towers, different cargo: send base-minus-finetuned activation differences across the bridge and ask what changed. That is model diffing.

predict.q: You paste the full sequence 'The capital of France is' and the oracle says 'Paris'. What have you shown?

options.t: Not much: it may have read the question, or the next-token guess
That the model plans its answers internally

predict.why: Full-sequence activations include the question, and the last position already encodes the next-token distribution. Rerun on a segment after ' France' and compare with the target's own top tokens.

predict.q: Why is the oracle usually a LoRA on the target's own base model?

options.t: It must already speak that activation space
LoRAs are the only way to run two models
So it can edit the target's weights

predict.why: Activations only make sense in the representation space they came from. A sibling of the same base model can read them as if they were its own tokens.

predict.q: A probe and an oracle both detect the secret. What does the probe give you that the oracle does not?

options.t: A direction you can test and intervene with
Answers to questions it was never trained on

predict.why: The probe answers one fixed question but hands you a direction, calibration and something to patch. The oracle answers anything, in prose only.

object.where: Anywhere one system reads another's internal state and reports in words: a diagnostic reader that explains a car's fault codes.
